findings.finding: Deployment is behind the company's own target. No BlueBird has launched since BlueBirds 11-13 on 2026-08-05, so 13 have launched and 12 work (BB7 was de-orbited). BlueBirds 14-16 reached Cape Canaveral around 2026-10-10 and still had no announced launch date on 2026-11-09. Reaching 'about 45 in orbit by early 2027' needs roughly 29-32 more satellites in 4-5 months. The 2026-11-06 8-K exhibit now frames external launch agreements as 'over 100 BlueBird satellites, to be deployed cumulatively between 2027 and 2028', so a formal cut or reframing of the early-2027 target on the call is likely. A near-term Falcon 9 date for 14-16 announced on the call would be the offsetting upside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-15: the target moved from 45-60 by end-2026 to about 45 by early 2027, in the same window as the $1B convert pricing, and the stock fell 17.0% (baseline). 2026-04-23: the BB7 orbit loss cost roughly 8-18%. 2026-10-13: Piper's downgrade to a forecast of 18 satellites by end-2026 cost 5-9%. findings.finding: The FY2026 revenue guide of $150-200M has been held unchanged for three reports and is now stretched. H1 was $46.3M (Q1 $14.7M, Q2 $31.5M). findings.finding: The Blacklift rocket was announced 2026-11-06 (8-K item 7.01). AST pays about $800M upfront ($400M cash plus 10-14M Class A shares, about 3.3-4.7% of 299.8M outstanding), $250M for engines for the first three rockets and $250M of engineering services over three years: more than $1.3B committed. First flights are late 2028, with a new US engine plant. The Q4 capex and cash guide on the call will have to absorb it, against negative free cash flow of $719M last quarter and pro forma cash of about $3.7B at June 30, before Q3 capex of $350-425M.
